questions.questionText: Which statement about the factors of production is correct?

options.text: Capital is a financial resource and includes savings in banks.
Enterprise is limited in supply and includes office workers.
Labour is a human resource and includes pensioners and children.
Land is a natural resource and includes trees and fish.

questions.questionText:
A builder spends one hour travelling to and from work. He works 40 hours per week for $200. He
is given a choice to work 50 hours a week for an extra $75.
What would be the opportunity cost to the builder of working the extra hours?

options.text: the ability to increase his purchasing power
the additional time travelling to and from work
the increased hourly earnings of $7.50
the ten hours of leisure time

questions.questionText: What is included in microeconomics?

options.text: the calculation of national income and expenditure
the effects of a change in exchange rates on the trade balance of an economy
the effects of an increase in the price of a good or service
the factors leading to demand-pull inflation

questions.questionText: What is an economist’s definition of a market?

options.text: a collection of informal retail outlets run by small firms
a place where traders gather regularly for short periods
a system that enables individuals and firms to buy and sell goods
the existence of consumer demand for a good

questions.questionText: What is an example of an external benefit from an individual cycling, rather than driving, to work?

options.text: higher cost of building cycle lanes
improved physical fitness to the individual from cycling
lower cost of cycling compared with driving to work
reduced congestion for other road users

questions.questionText:
It is expected that consumers will use less paper money.
What is the most likely reason for this?

options.text: Inflation reduces the value of paper money.
More ways of making payments will be available.
Other forms of money are more durable.
Paper money will have less intrinsic value.

questions.questionText:
In low-income countries, fewer girls than boys become skilled design engineers.
What might explain this situation?

options.text: Girls are only interested in low-wage jobs.
Girls do not favour heavy manual work.
Girls have fewer opportunities to complete higher education.
It costs more for girls to be trained as design engineers.

questions.questionText:
A company mining cobalt, invests in machinery to replace some workers. Eventually diseconomies
of scale occur.
What could cause this situation?

options.text: As more cobalt is mined average costs increase.
Fewer workers are needed to produce the required output.
Output per hour increases as more machinery is used.
Overhead costs are spread as output increases.

questions.questionText: Why are many hairdressers able to operate as small businesses?

options.text: high level of competition
high scope for economies of scale
long period of training required
low start-up and running costs

questions.questionText:
Dimitry owns a firm that produces and sells bottles of lemonade. He only sells one size of bottle.
How would Dimitry calculate the total revenue of the firm?

options.text: multiply the quantity sold by the cost per bottle
multiply the quantity sold by the price per bottle
multiply the quantity sold by the profit per bottle
multiply the quantity sold by the tax per bottle

questions.questionText:
Which market is likely to be the most competitive?
barriers number
to entry of sellers

options.text: high few
high many
low few
low many

questions.questionText:
An economy has a high rate of inflation. In response to this, its government increases income tax.
What is the most likely reason for this increase?

options.text: to discourage the consumption of harmful goods
to raise money for government spending
to redistribute income
to reduce total demand

questions.questionText:
Interest rates are sometimes raised to control inflation.
Why might this policy be effective?

options.text: Consumers may save more.
Government spending may increase.
Investment may be encouraged.
The exchange rate may fall.

questions.questionText:
A government’s revenue grew 8% to $3.25 trillion. Its expenditure was reduced to $3.69 trillion.
What can be concluded from this?
government
state of budget
policy aim

options.text: deficit increase deficit
deficit reduce deficit
surplus increase surplus
surplus reduce surplus

questions.questionText:
A country’s inflation rate, measured by the Consumer Prices Index (CPI), was 3% in year 1.
Three years later it was 0.8%.
What can be concluded from this information?

options.text: Prices are falling.
The rate of price increases is falling.
The real rate of interest is negative.
There is increased purchasing power for those on fixed incomes.

questions.questionText: What will deflation most likely lead to?

options.text: a fall in the real value of debts
an increase in the exchange rate
an increase in the rate of interest
an increase in the real purchasing power of money

questions.questionText: Economic growth can be defined as

options.text: a reduction in a country’s rate of inflation.
an increase in a country’s exports.
an increase in a country’s population.
an increase in a country’s productive capacity.

questions.questionText:
The table compares the distribution of employment in selected industries in two years.
employment in millions
industry
year 1 year 2
agriculture 4 3
mining 2 2
manufacturing 6 6
retailing 4 4
transport 4 5
total 20 20
How did the distribution of employment change between year 1 and year 2?
primary sector secondary sector

options.text: fell rose
fell unchanged
rose fell
rose unchanged

questions.questionText:
In a year, two changes occurred in a company.
Company directors’ salaries increased by 15%.
Office workers’ wages increased by 5%.
The rate of inflation was 3.4%.
What happened to real income?
company directors’ office workers’
real income real income

options.text: fell fell
fell rose
rose fell
rose rose

questions.questionText:
The richest 60% of the population of a high-income economy received an increase in income.
The income of the rest of the population did not change.
What happened to absolute and relative poverty?
absolute poverty relative poverty

options.text: increased increased
increased remained constant
remained constant increased
remained constant remained constant

questions.questionText:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is a better measure of comparative living standards when it is
adjusted for the effects of

options.text: exports and inflation.
imports and exports.
population change and exports.
population change and inflation.

questions.questionText: What is a disadvantage of increasing international specialisation?

options.text: Consumers pay higher prices for goods and services reducing their welfare.
Domestic firms may be uncompetitive leading to structural unemployment.
Domestic firms may experience rising costs as they pay more for imports.
Resources may be used less efficiently as domestic firms face less competition.

questions.questionText: Which method of protection always reduces the supply of an imported good to zero?

options.text: embargo
quota
subsidy
tariff

questions.questionText:
A country has a deficit on its current account of its balance of payments.
What could increase the size of its deficit?

options.text: increased exports of its services
increased international competitiveness of its goods
increased numbers of visitors from abroad
